WITH step1 AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY o.customer_id, c.gender
),
step2 AS (
  SELECT gender, SUM(order_count) as total_orders_per_gender
  FROM step1
  GROUP BY gender
),
step3 AS (
  SELECT step1.customer_id, step1.gender, step1.order_count, 
         CAST(step1.order_count AS REAL) / step2.total_orders_per_gender as ratio
  FROM step1 JOIN step2 ON step1.gender = step2.gender
),
step4 AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) as avg_ratio FROM step3
)
SELECT step3.customer_id, step3.gender, step3.order_count, step3.ratio,
       step3.ratio - step4.avg_ratio as difference
FROM step3, step4
WHERE step3.ratio > step4.avg_ratio
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 10
